cards.title: Under fire
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: The piece shows the security challenge in KP and the frontline role of the provincial police in counter-terrorism.
cards.summary: Dawn's editorial says at least 12 policemen were martyred in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in one day. Ten died in an ambush in Kohat and two in Swabi, while a vehicle bomb attack on a police station in Dera Ismail Khan was repelled. The paper says attacks on police are becoming deadlier, and the force lacks enough personnel, arms and equipment. It asks the centre, which now controls the province, to fund the police fully and fill vacant posts.
key_facts: At least 12 policemen were martyred in KP in a single day: 10 in Kohat and 2 in Swabi.
The Kohat police team was ambushed in the Darbukach area after a joint operation against illegal gold mining.
At least 18 attackers were killed when the police fought back in Kohat.
An explosive-laden pickup hit the gate of a police station in Dera Ismail Khan, but the attack was repelled with no police casualties.
Official data shows police deaths and injuries in the first half of the year doubled from the year before, while attacks rose by 34pc.

vocab.meaning: continuing without becoming weaker
the authority of the state to enforce its rule

text: THE bloodshed continues unabated. On Wednesday, at least 12 policemen were martyred in the line of duty in KP. Ten lives were lost in an ambush in Kohat while a police party was returning from a clearance operation, and two more were martyred in Swabi when a police patrol came under fire.

Separately, an explosive-laden pickup slammed into the main gate of a police station in Dera Ismail Khan, but the attack was promptly repelled. Thankfully, no police casualties were reported in the latter incident. Still, a dozen lives lost in a single day and at least a dozen more injured and hospitalised is a heavy toll for a provincial police force engaged in a relentless, fierce fight against terrorists threatening the state’s writ every day. The Kohat ambush, in particular, appears to have been a major security incident. By police accounts, a team that conducted a joint operation with the civil administration against illegal gold mining in the Darbukach area was returning after completing its objectives when it was ambushed by what appears to have been a very large group. At least 18 attackers were killed as the police fought back.

Official data shows that police fatalities and injuries in the first half of this year alone had doubled from the year before. The number of attacks, on the other hand, had risen by 34pc. The data suggests that attacks on police have become increasingly deadly, and, coupled with shortfalls in personnel, arms and necessary equipment, the KP police are increasingly vulnerable as they play a frontline role in ongoing operations against terrorists.

Though October saw a marked improvement in the number of attacks compared to just a month earlier, the three incidents on Wednesday underline how fragile those gains can be if the police are not strengthened while the state has the upper hand. After the centre took control of the province, it bears full responsibility for the police’s protection. The new administration appointed to oversee KP’s affairs must immediately ensure that the provincial security forces receive all the funds they have requested and fill vacant posts on an urgent basis. It must ensure armoured vehicles, protective equipment, night-vision devices and better weapons are supplied to frontline personnel, and that intelligence and army backup are available during police operations in high-risk areas.
Published in Dawn, November 13th, 2026

cards.title: Climate challenges
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: It links smog, climate adaptation and Pakistan's COP31 energy pledges, a frequent theme in environment and essay papers.
cards.summary: Dawn's editorial says Punjab's smog points to a wider climate crisis that cannot be solved with small, scattered steps. Floods, heatwaves and water stress are all connected. It welcomes the clean energy goals the prime minister set out at COP31, but says an energy transition alone is not a climate policy. Pakistan must also enforce emission rules, protect communities and adapt farming.
key_facts: Lahore's air quality index stood at a hazardous 358 on a Wednesday in November 2026.
At COP31, PM Shehbaz Sharif said Pakistan added nearly 22 gigawatts of rooftop solar capacity in two years.
Pakistan has backed a pledge to raise electricity's share of energy use to 35pc by 2035.
Pakistan aims for electric vehicles to make up 30pc of new vehicle sales by 2030.
The prime minister called for concessional finance and affordable technology for vulnerable nations.

vocab.meaning: done in small, separate parts, not as a whole plan
given on easier terms than normal, such as low-interest loans

text: THE poisonous smog blanketing Punjab is an immediate threat to public health, but it also points to a larger environmental crisis that Pakistan can no longer address through piecemeal measures. Lahore’s air quality index stood at a hazardous 358 on Wednesday, while other cities struggled under the same toxic haze.

Punjab’s government says better monitoring and enforcement have brought improvements over previous years. That is welcome, but the air remains dangerous. While pollution from India compounds the problem, Pakistan must also confront domestic emissions.

Moreover, smog is not the country’s only warning. Our climate crises are deeply interconnected. Repeated floods, punishing heatwaves and mounting water stress show how exposed Pakistan is to climate shocks, and how urgently it needs lasting solutions.

At COP31, PM Shehbaz Sharif outlined a cleaner energy future that deserves support. He pointed to nearly 22 gigawatts of rooftop solar capacity added in two years, much of it driven by households seeking relief from expensive electricity.

Pakistan has backed a pledge to increase electricity’s share of energy use to 35pc by 2035 and aims for electric vehicles to account for 30pc of new vehicle sales by 2030. These shifts could help reduce fossil-fuel dependence and, especially through cleaner transport, cut harmful emissions. But an energy transition is not, by itself, a climate policy.

Pakistan also needs to protect communities from floods and extreme heat, safeguard water supplies and adapt agriculture to changing conditions. The PM rightly called for concessional finance and affordable technology. Rich industrialised countries bear much of the responsibility for global warming and must help vulnerable nations cope. Yet appeals for international climate justice must run alongside serious action at home.

That action requires more than ambitious targets or seasonal restrictions. Authorities must enforce vehicle and industrial emission standards, expand public transport, support farmers in ending crop burning and make clean technology accessible beyond affluent households. Cities must be better prepared for floods and extreme weather, while rural communities need help coping with rising temperatures and water shortages.

Federal and provincial governments must work together and ensure that environmental regulations are properly enforced. Businesses, too, must reduce their environmental impact, while citizens have a responsibility to conserve resources, avoid polluting their surroundings and demand action from the state.

None of this will be easy in a country facing serious fiscal constraints. But the cost of delay is already being paid in illness, damaged livelihoods and repeated disruption. Pakistan cannot afford to confront its climate crises one disaster, one season and one international summit at a time.
Published in Dawn, November 13th, 2026

cards.title: Constrained partnership
cards.author: Zafar Mirza
cards.why: It is a useful case study of health governance, donor dependence and Pakistan's HIV and TB challenge.
cards.summary: Former health minister Zafar Mirza writes about Pakistan's troubled ties with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. In August 2020 the Fund placed Pakistan under its Additional Safeguard Policy (ASP) because it lost confidence in how Pakistan managed its grants. He links this to weak governance, frequent changes of leadership and a sharp rise in HIV infections. He calls for a time-bound plan to exit ASP and a gradual move to more domestic funding.
key_facts: Since 2003, the Global Fund has given more than $1.1 billion to Pakistan's HIV, TB and malaria programmes.
The Global Fund invoked its Additional Safeguard Policy on Pakistan in August 2020, through a letter dated Aug 6, 2020.
The Global Fund was set up in 2002 and has helped save an estimated 72 million lives globally.
The ASP was adopted in 2004 and has been used in about 30 countries but revoked in only three: Cuba, Myanmar and Côte d'Ivoire.
According to WHO and UNAIDS estimates, new HIV infections in Pakistan rose from about 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024.
In 2024, 90pc of Pakistan's HIV financing came from the Global Fund.

vocab.meaning: related to how diseases spread in a population
officially cancelled

text: “Trust takes years to build, seconds to break, and forever to repair.” Anonymous
THIS observation aptly describes Pakistan’s relationship with one of its most important international health partners.

Since 2003, the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tu­­berculosis and Malaria has disbursed more than $1.1 billion to Pakistan’s HIV, tuberculosis and malaria programmes. In August 2020, however, it invoked its Additional Safeguard Policy (ASP) on Pakistan.

Behind this bureaucratic terminology lies an extraordinary decision: the Global Fund no longer had sufficient confidence in the country’s arrangements for managing its gra­nts and implementing disease-control programmes.
More than six years later, this decision deserves serious public scrutiny.

Established in 2002, the Global Fund is one of the most successful innovations in international health financing. It mobilises resources to support countries fighting these three diseases and has helped save an estimated 72 million lives globally. Pakistan has been a significant beneficiary.

The Global Fund normally operates through a partnership model in which national stakeholders identify priorities, nominate implementing organisations and oversee grants through a Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM). The underlying philosophy is country ownership: international resources should strengthen national institutions, not substitute for them.
The Global Fund’s observations point to serious weaknesses in governance & institutional accountability.

In 2004, the Global Fund Board adopted ASP to address situations where normal funding arrangements could not adequately protect its investments. It permits oversight and direct involvement in selecting principal recipients and implementing partners. In effect, decisions normally taken by national institutions can be assumed by the international financing agency.

This is an exceptional, temporary arrangement, reflecting serious concerns about governance, institutional capacity, accountability or programme implementation. Since its introduction, it has been invoked in around 30 countries but revoked in only three: Cuba, Myanmar and Côte d’Ivoire. This shows that entering ASP is easier than exiting it.
Why was Pakistan placed under ASP? The ans­wer lies in a candid letter dated Aug 6, 2020, from the Global Fund to the Pakistan government.

It expressed serious dissatisfaction with Pakistan’s response to HIV and TB, noting stagnating or declining TB notifications and an almost unchecked increase in HIV incidence. Significantly, it stated that public-sector principal recipients had failed to translate domestic and external financing into effective programmes.

The letter specifically criticised the performance of the Common Management Unit (CMU), responsible for coordinating the three disease programmes, and identified inadequate leadership in managing challenges arising from devolution.

These observations point to serious weaknesses in governance, leadership, coordination and institutional accountability. Consider this: Between 2020 and 2022, Pakistan changed the national coordinator of the CMU 10 times in three years. Many appointments were political.

The epidemiological consequences are equally troubling. While many states have reduced new HIV infections, Pakistan has moved in the opposite direction. According to WHO and UNAIDS estimates reported in Dec 2025, annual new infections increased from approximately 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024 — a 200pc increase.

ASP’s implications extend beyond these programmes. For a country seeking international inv­estment, development assistance and credibility in global institutions, its inability to demonstrate satisfactory governance of externally financed hea­­lth programmes sends a deeply damaging message.

But ASP should not be viewed merely as an international embarrassment. Its more serious implication is the erosion of national ownership. When external partners increasingly determine arrangements, domestic institutions risk becoming less accountable for results.
Pakistan must therefore develop a credible, time-bound roadmap for exiting ASP.

The Aug 2020 letter identified the conditions for its revocation: timely provincial budget disbursements for HIV and TB; satisfactory programme performance and financial risk management; demonstrated political commitment; compliance with audit recommendations, etc.
These are not unreasonable demands.
Federal and provincial governments must jointly establish a high-level mechanism to monitor progress against each condition through independently verifiable indicators.
Civil society and affected communities must also be meaningfully engaged.
There is another dimension requiring urgent attention: financial sustainability.

For over two decades, Pakistan has depended heavily on the Global Fund for essential components of its HIV, TB and malaria responses. In 2024, 90pc of HIV financing came from the Fund. This assistance has been invaluable. But indefinite dependence on external financing is neither desirable nor realistic, particularly as international development assistance comes under increasing pressure.

Pakistan needs a carefully planned transition towards greater domestic financial responsibility. This does not mean abruptly replacing Global Fund resources or imposing unaffordable obligations on provincial governments overnight.

The FCDO-financed, Oxford Policy Managem­e­nt-implemented Global Fund Accelerator Prog­ra­mme is providing valuable analytical support and recommendations. Federal and provincial governments must make optimal use of this opportunity.

They should negotiate a gradual increase in domestic financing. Public financing should progressively assume responsibility for recurrent expenditures, while increasingly covering medicines and prevention services.
Crucially, exiting ASP and transitioning from donor dependence are related but distinct processes.

The Global Fund has stood by Pakistan through successive health emergencies and institutional challenges. Its continued engagement, even after invoking ASP, demonstrates that its objective is not to abandon Pakistan but to protect investments and improve results. Pakistan must respond with the seriousness this partnership deserves.

Ultimately, the most compelling argument for reform is not the restoration of international prestige. It is the right of millions of Pakistanis to effective prevention, diagnosis and treatment. The real achievement will be transforming a constrained partnership into a confident, accountable and genuinely country-owned response to three preventable and treatable diseases.
The writer is a former health minister, adjunct professor of health systems and population health, president of Pakistan Association of Lifestyle Medicine and convener of Lok Sehat.
Published in Dawn, November 13th, 2026

cards.title: Referendum for new provinces
cards.author: editorial
cards.why: New provinces, devolution and the constitutional rules on referendums are core Pakistan Affairs topics.
cards.summary: The Express Tribune supports the idea of a referendum on creating new provinces, put forward by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. It argues that Pakistan needs more devolution for better governance and fairer sharing of resources. But it warns that Pakistan's past referendums lacked credibility. It says the vote must be free and fair, and the electoral watchdog should be reconstituted.
key_facts: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi proposed a referendum to seek public opinion on creating new provinces.
The editorial says such a referendum would be held under Article 48(6) and Article 48(7) of the Constitution.
Some experts say creating a new province still formally requires a constitutional amendment under Article 239.
Under the proposal, the referendum would need approval in a joint sitting of Parliament.

vocab.meaning: an essential condition
narrow, local-minded thinking
affected by bad experience; distrustful

text: Amidst persisting differences among the political parties over the creation of new provinces, or more administrative units, the idea of holding a referendum seems to be well on track. It is a foregone conclusion that Pakistan is in dire need of the devolution of powers and an organic grassroots structure to address the socio-economic problems of a soaring population. This is a sine qua non not only for ushering in good governance, but also for ensuring that public service delivery is satisfactory and the present disparities in the sharing of resources are done away with. It is, however, also a reality that all major political forces had, in principle, canvassed for more provinces. At this juncture, yet some beg to differ – either on the modus operandi or to further their self-serving agendas. Thus, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's suggestion of opting for a referendum to elicit public opinion on such a sensitive national issue is a constitutionally viable way out. The million-dollar question is whether the proposed referendum will be transparent and impartial, or whether it will merely add to the sordid episodes of yesteryears when genuine public opinion was thrown to the wind to preserve an entrenched status quo. Pakistan has a jaundiced history of referendums. Such ballots in the past were solely dictatorial in essence and are widely mocked for lacking credibility. Thus, the proposed referendum on new provinces must be different; it should be an exercise that unites the nation rather than sows seeds of parochialism and dissent. Held under Article 48(6) and Article 48(7), the referendum must transparently pass through the test of popular approval in a joint sitting of Parliament and be executed in all sincerity through a free and fair ballot. Some experts, however, insist that creating a new province still formally requires a constitutional amendment under Article 239. Even so, a credible referendum could generate the overwhelming public mandate needed to compel reluctant lawmakers to pass the requisite legislation The interior minister, who kicked off the debate by stating that the system has collapsed and a reset is desired, must go the extra mile to take along all political segments to assure them that the referendum will be non-partisan and thoroughly fair. Reconstituting the electoral watchdog is a must to exhibit sincerity of purpose. Let the fragmented national canvas unite on a single consensus of sharing power through devolution, and let the raison d'être be development and empowerment for all.

cards.title: Population emergency
cards.author: editorial
cards.why: Population is a recurring essay and Pakistan Affairs topic, linked to the NFC Award and human development.
cards.summary: The Express Tribune says population growth has become so fast that economic growth cannot keep up. The National Population Council has called it a national emergency. The paper blames poor female education and limited access to contraception. It asks for a review of the NFC formula and a National Population Stabilisation Programme.
key_facts: The National Population Council has declared rapid population growth a national emergency.
The 2023 census recorded Pakistan's population at 241.5 million.
The 2023 census put the annual growth rate at 2.55%.
The current National Finance Commission formula gives 82% weightage to population.

vocab.meaning: economic gain possible when the working-age share of the population is large

text: Pakistan's population crisis has reached a point where economic growth can no longer compensate for the relentless increase in pressure on limited resources. The National Population Council has recognised that rapid population growth has become a national emergency. The 2023 census recorded a population of 241.5 million, growing annually at 2.55%. This reversal points towards a failure to integrate population management into national development priorities. The consequences are evident in the widening gap between public expenditure and service delivery. Millions of children remain out of school while healthcare facilities are insufficient. Morover, employment opportunities cannot accommodate the expanding workforce. Even sustained economic expansion offers limited improvements in living standards when population growth absorbs much of its benefits. Yet the challenge extends beyond birth rates. Inadequate female education and restricted reproductive healthcare coupled with limited access to contraception undermine efforts towards population stabilisation. The existing National Finance Commission formula, which assigns 82% weightage to population, also warrants reconsideration. Resource distribution must encourage improvements in human development without penalising provinces struggling with larger populations. Pakistan desperately requires a National Population Stabilisation Programme to ensure accessible family planning service initiatives with measurable outcomes. Without decisive intervention, the demographic dividend will remain unrealised, while mounting demands on education, healthcare, employment and public resources will continue to undermine economic progress and national development.

cards.title: The Case for a Trump-Xi-Putin Summit
cards.author: Charles Kupchan
cards.why: It shows great-power diplomacy over the Ukraine war, relevant to International Relations papers.
cards.summary: In Foreign Affairs, Charles Kupchan discusses a possible three-way summit of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China. Putin reportedly suggested the idea to discuss ending the Ukraine war. The idea has caused alarm in Europe and in the US Congress. The headline shows Kupchan argues in favour of such a meeting.
key_facts: The APEC meeting in November 2026 was due to be held in Shenzhen, China.
According to The Wall Street Journal, Putin floated the idea of a three-way summit to discuss ending the war in Ukraine.
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski warned against a repeat of the 1945 Yalta Conference.
US Senator Chris Coons said there can be no talks on Ukraine's future "without Ukraine at the table".

vocab.meaning: shock and worry
talks among three parties

text: In just a few days’ time, U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin could be holding a three-way summit on the sidelines of next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen, China. According to The Wall Street Journal, Putin floated the idea of a trialogue last month as an opportunity to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. No firm plan has yet been announced, but even the prospect of this meeting has provoked widespread consternation. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski warned against a repeat of the Yalta Conference of 1945, when U.S. President Franklin Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill capitulated to Soviet leader Joseph Stalin’s push for the Soviet Union to dominate Eastern Europe. U.S. Senator Chris Coons posted on X that “there can be no talks about Ukraine’s future without Ukraine at the table, and there can be no real negotiations as long as Trump signals weakness and servitude to Xi and Putin at every opportunity.”

cards.title: The World’s Last Chance for Peace
cards.author: Pedro Sánchez
cards.why: It gives a European leader's view on global peace, useful for International Relations essays.
cards.summary: From the published summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez writes in Foreign Affairs about how the world can avoid a new world war. He presents this as the world's last chance for peace.
key_facts: Pedro Sánchez wrote a Foreign Affairs piece titled "The World's Last Chance for Peace".

cards.title: Beyond diplomacy
cards.author: Laraib Sajid
cards.why: It links economic diplomacy, the SIFC and federalism after the 18th Amendment.
cards.summary: Lawyer Laraib Sajid says Pakistan's diplomatic gains, including mediating between the US and Iran, must turn into real investment. The SIFC has a large project pipeline, but investors look at legal and administrative conditions. After the 18th Amendment, many sectors like minerals, tourism and agriculture need provincial approval, and the SIFC cannot direct provinces. She suggests using existing bodies such as the Interprovincial Coordination Committee and Provincial Investment Committees.
key_facts: The SIFC presented a pipeline of 38 projects worth about $40 billion in potential investment to a Senate committee.
The SIFC was formed in 2023 through an amendment to the Board of Investment Ordinance, 2001.
Section 10E of the BOI Ordinance lets the SIFC direct federal bodies but does not expressly cover provincial governments.
Provincial Investment Committees are set up under Section 15 of the BOI Ordinance.
The 18th Amendment strengthened provincial autonomy by moving responsibilities from the centre to the provinces.

vocab.meaning: points where progress is slowed or blocked

cards.title: Ambition without scale?
cards.author: Ehsan Malik
cards.why: It covers industrial policy, localisation and trade rules relevant to Economy papers.
cards.summary: Ehsan Malik, former head of Unilever Pakistan, reviews the new Auto Policy 2026-31. He welcomes its aim of making the industry competitive but warns that cutting tariffs too fast could destroy the skills of local parts makers. He says too many models keep volumes low and costs high, and export targets need real buyers. He also questions the proposed Automotive Development Levy.
key_facts: Pakistan announced an Auto Policy for 2026-31.
The policy envisages about $6 billion in cumulative automotive exports over five years.
The proposed Automotive Development Levy is expected to raise Rs232bn over five years.
WTO rules restrict subsidies that depend on export performance.
Auto-part industrial clusters exist around Port Qasim and Lahore-Sheikhupura.

vocab.meaning: extra import taxes to offset unfair foreign subsidies
making parts within the country instead of importing them

cards.title: Used car imports
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: It connects imports, the external account and local industry, useful for Economy questions.
cards.summary: Dawn's editorial says the government's effort to curb used car imports is failing. Even after the personal baggage scheme was abolished, cars keep coming through the gift scheme meant for overseas Pakistanis. This drains foreign exchange, loses tax revenue and hurts the local auto parts industry. The paper says the new auto policy may add to this damage.
key_facts: The personal baggage scheme for used car imports has been abolished.
More than 2,000 used vehicles reportedly arrived through the gift scheme in October 2026.
Imports of completely built-up (CBU) vehicles rose 40pc to $126m in the first quarter of FY2026-27.

vocab.meaning: losing strength; starting to fail

cards.title: Pakistan announces 13 mineral cooperation deals
cards.author: Shahbaz Rana
cards.why: Mineral development and foreign investment are key Pakistan economy and Balochistan topics.
cards.summary: At the end of the Pakistan Mineral Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad, Pakistan announced 13 agreements with foreign firms and countries. PM Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir said Pakistan wants full value chains, not raw mineral exports. Barrick Gold said it would stay a long-term partner in Reko Diq. Many deals involve Turkish, British, American, German and Japanese partners, mostly for Chagai and Pishin in Balochistan.
key_facts: Pakistan finalised 13 joint ventures, MoUs and agreements at the Pakistan Mineral Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad.
Barrick Gold, which owns 50% of the Reko Diq project, said it intends to remain a long-term partner of Pakistan.
The FWO and Ivanhoe Mines signed an MoU for mineral exploration and mining in Chagai, Balochistan.
Turkiye's MTA International Company and PMDC signed a joint venture to explore antimony, copper, gold and other minerals in Pishin, Balochistan.
According to ICMA, Pakistan's mineral reserves are worth about $8 trillion over 600,000 square kilometres.
Mining has historically contributed less than 3% to Pakistan's GDP.

vocab.meaning: all the steps from raw material to finished product
testing a mineral to find what it contains

cards.title: Copper, gold deposits identified at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district: mining company
cards.author: Khaleeq Kiani
cards.why: It shows private-sector progress in Pakistan's mineral exploration in Balochistan.
cards.summary: National Resources Limited (NRL) says it has found copper and gold deposits at eight sites in Chagai, Balochistan, after about 25,000 metres of drilling. The finds lie in Darigwan, next to its earlier Tang Kaur discovery. The company is preparing its first formal resource estimate under international standards. It plans further studies from 2027 and a bankable feasibility study by the end of the decade.
key_facts: NRL identified copper and gold deposits at eight sites in Chagai district after nearly 25,000 metres of drilling.
One drill hole showed a 295-metre stretch with 0.43pc copper and 0.13 grams of gold per tonne.
The discoveries cover 5.6 square kilometres in Darigwan, next to the Tang Kaur copper-gold site.
NRL is a joint venture of Fatima Fertilisers, Liberty Mills and Lucky Cement and holds five exploration licences in Balochistan.
NRL has committed $100 million to mineral exploration in Pakistan.
NRL has partnered with LUMS to build a predictive AI model for exploration.

vocab.meaning: a detailed study strong enough for banks to lend money for a project

cards.title: Pakistan calls for ‘immediate’ end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as UNSC renews Yemen sanctions
cards.author: Anwar Iqbal
cards.why: It shows Pakistan's stance on Saudi security and the working of UN sanctions regimes.
cards.summary: The UN Security Council renewed sanctions on those threatening peace in Yemen, including people linked to the Houthis, by consensus. The resolution also aims to stop the Houthis getting parts and chemicals for drones and missiles. Pakistan's envoy condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and demanded they stop at once. Pakistan also called for a Yemeni-led political process under the UN.
key_facts: The UNSC extended the asset freeze and travel ban in the Yemen sanctions regime until Nov 14, 2027.
The mandate of the Panel of Experts monitoring Yemen sanctions was renewed until Dec 15, 2027.
The arms embargo under Resolution 2216 of April 2015 has no expiry date.
Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN is Ambassador Syed Haider Shah.
The Houthis seized Sanaa in 2014, and Saudi Arabia intervened militarily in 2015.
The Bab el-Mandeb Strait links the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

vocab.meaning: chemicals used to make other substances, such as explosives
deserving strong blame

cards.title: National Population Council says rapid population growth a national emergency
cards.why: It marks an official recognition of the population crisis, a common essay theme.
cards.summary: From the published summary: The National Population Council has declared rapid population growth a national emergency in Pakistan.
key_facts: The National Population Council termed rapid population growth a national emergency.

cards.title: Judges close part of ICC Afghanistan investigations that could look at US troops
cards.author: Reuters
cards.why: It concerns international justice, the ICC's jurisdiction and US-ICC tensions.
cards.summary: ICC judges have formally closed the part of the Afghanistan investigation that could have examined alleged crimes by US troops, and a probe into ISIS-K. The court will now focus only on Taliban actions since 2021. The prosecutor's office has appealed. Arrest warrants against four Taliban leaders remain in force.
key_facts: ICC judges closed the Afghanistan inquiry line on alleged crimes by US troops and on ISIS-K.
The remaining ICC Afghanistan case focuses on Taliban actions since 2021.
ICC arrest warrants against four Afghan Taliban leaders remain in effect.
The US has imposed sanctions on the ICC, citing warrants for Israeli officials and the probe into US soldiers.
The ICC can prosecute atrocity crimes committed on the territory of its member states.

vocab.meaning: inactive for a time

cards.title: UN chief urges drastic emissions cuts as COP31 wrestles with fossil fuels
cards.author: Reuters
cards.why: COP31 outcomes and global climate politics are central to Environment and Current Affairs papers.
cards.summary: UN chief Antonio Guterres called for immediate and drastic emission cuts as the first week of COP31 in Turkiye ended. Oil producers and large developing economies are resisting firm targets on fossil fuels. Host Turkiye wants global electrification at the centre of the deal, while Australia leads the negotiations. The US skipped the talks for a second year.
key_facts: COP31 is being held in Turkiye, with Australia as lead negotiator under a split presidency.
Guterres is leaving office at the end of December 2026 after two five-year terms.
The US skipped the COP talks for a second year in a row under President Trump.
A glacier collapse in Nepal in 2026 triggered a flood that killed more than 1,450 people.
The 1.5°C warming limit was agreed under the 2015 Paris Agreement.
Brazil hosted the previous year's COP.

vocab.meaning: switching machines and energy use to electricity

cards.title: OECD report reveals migration to developed countries is dwindling
cards.author: AFP
cards.why: It gives data on global migration trends, relevant to International Affairs and Pakistan's overseas workforce.
cards.summary: An OECD report says migration to its 38 member countries fell for a second year in 2025. New permanent immigrants fell to 6.1 million from 6.2 million. Humanitarian migration dropped sharply, while labour migration rose. Portugal, Spain and Italy saw big rises, while the US, Canada and the UK saw falls.
key_facts: OECD countries recorded 6.1 million new permanent immigrants in 2025, down 1.6pc from 6.2 million.
Legal humanitarian migration to OECD countries fell 26pc in 2025, while labour migration rose 13pc.
Portugal saw a 139pc rise in permanent migrants in 2025, to 313,600.
The US still led OECD countries with over 1.2 million permanent migrants despite a 14pc fall.
India was the leading country of origin for migration to the OECD in 2024, ahead of China and Colombia.
The OECD working-age population is set to fall by 8pc by 2060.

mcqs.q: In November 2026, the UN Security Council extended the asset freeze and travel ban under its Yemen sanctions regime until which date?
mcqs.explanation: The resolution, adopted by consensus, extended the asset freeze and travel ban until Nov 14, 2027; the Panel of Experts mandate runs to Dec 15, 2027. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: The UN arms embargo on Yemen's Houthis, which has no expiry date, was imposed under which Security Council resolution of April 2015?
mcqs.explanation: Resolution 2216 of April 2015 imposed the arms embargo; the Council reaffirmed it in November 2026. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: Who was Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN who condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia at the Security Council in November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Ambassador Syed Haider Shah demanded an immediate and unconditional end to Houthi attacks and called for a Yemeni-led political process. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, threatened by the Houthi escalation in 2026, links which two bodies of water?
options: Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
Arabian Sea and Gulf of Aden
Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
mcqs.explanation: The Bab el-Mandeb is a key shipping route linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: Which country hosted the COP31 climate talks held in November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: COP31 was held in Turkiye, which pushed a global electrification proposal; Brazil hosted the previous year's COP. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: Under the split presidency arrangement at COP31 in 2026, which country served as lead negotiator?
mcqs.explanation: Australia led the negotiations while Turkiye hosted the summit, and Australia was drafting a political text to be agreed by consensus. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: According to an OECD report released in November 2026, how many new permanent immigrants did OECD countries record in 2025?
mcqs.explanation: OECD countries recorded 6.1 million new permanent immigrants in 2025, down 1.6pc from 6.2 million the year before. (Dawn/AFP)

mcqs.q: Which OECD country saw the largest rise in permanent migrants in 2025, an increase of 139pc?
mcqs.explanation: Portugal's permanent migrants rose 139pc to 313,600, mainly due to approval of a backlog of residency permits. (Dawn/AFP)

mcqs.q: According to the OECD, which country was the leading country of origin for migration to OECD countries in 2024?
mcqs.explanation: India was the top source of migratory flows to the OECD in 2024, ahead of China and Colombia. (Dawn/AFP)

mcqs.q: How many member countries does the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) have?
mcqs.explanation: The OECD has 38 member countries; its 2026 migration report covered flows to all of them. (Dawn/AFP)

mcqs.q: After ICC judges closed parts of the Afghanistan investigation in 2026, arrest warrants remained in effect against how many Afghan Taliban leaders?
mcqs.explanation: Judges closed the inquiry lines covering US troops and ISIS-K, but warrants against four Taliban leaders remain in effect; the prosecutor appealed. (Dawn/Reuters)

mcqs.q: When did the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria place Pakistan under its Additional Safeguard Policy?
mcqs.explanation: The Global Fund invoked the ASP on Pakistan in August 2020, citing weak performance in HIV and TB programmes. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: The Global Fund's Additional Safeguard Policy has been revoked in only three countries. Which of these is one of them?
mcqs.explanation: The ASP, adopted in 2004, has been invoked in about 30 countries but revoked only in Cuba, Myanmar and Côte d'Ivoire. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: According to WHO and UNAIDS estimates, roughly how many new HIV infections did Pakistan record in 2024?
mcqs.explanation: New HIV infections in Pakistan rose from about 16,000 in 2010 to 48,000 in 2024, a 200pc increase. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: According to the 2023 census, what was Pakistan's annual population growth rate?
mcqs.explanation: The 2023 census put the population at 241.5 million, growing at 2.55% a year; the National Population Council has called this a national emergency. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: What weightage does the current National Finance Commission formula give to population in distributing resources among provinces?
mcqs.explanation: The NFC formula assigns 82% weightage to population, which critics say should be reconsidered. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) was set up in 2023 through an amendment to which law?
mcqs.explanation: The SIFC was created in 2023 by amending the BOI Ordinance, 2001; Section 10E lets it direct federal bodies. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: Under Pakistan's Auto Policy 2026-31, the proposed Automotive Development Levy is expected to raise how much over five years?
mcqs.explanation: The levy is expected to raise Rs232bn over five years; the policy also targets about $6bn in auto exports. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: How many agreements, joint ventures and MoUs were finalised at the close of the Pakistan Mineral Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan announced 13 mineral cooperation deals, aiming to move away from exporting raw minerals. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: What share of the Reko Diq project is owned by Barrick Gold?
mcqs.explanation: Barrick Gold owns 50% of Reko Diq; its chairman John Thornton said in November 2026 it would remain a long-term partner. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: According to the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants (ICMA), Pakistan's mineral reserves are estimated to be worth about how much?
mcqs.explanation: ICMA estimates Pakistan's mineral reserves at about $8 trillion, spread over 600,000 square kilometres. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: In 2026, National Resources Limited partnered with which university to develop a predictive AI model for mineral exploration in Balochistan?
mcqs.explanation: NRL, a venture of Fatima Fertilisers, Liberty Mills and Lucky Cement, teamed up with LUMS on an AI exploration model. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: In November 2026, Turkiye's MTA International Company and the Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation signed a joint venture to explore antimony, copper and gold in which district of Balochistan?
mcqs.explanation: The MTAIC-PMDC venture covers antimony, copper, gold, silver, molybdenum and other critical minerals in Pishin. (The Express Tribune)

mcqs.q: At COP31 in 2026, PM Shehbaz Sharif said Pakistan had added nearly how much rooftop solar capacity in two years?
mcqs.explanation: The prime minister cited nearly 22GW of rooftop solar added in two years, largely by households facing costly electricity. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: What share of new vehicle sales does Pakistan aim to have as electric vehicles by 2030?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan targets 30pc of new vehicle sales to be electric by 2030 and backs raising electricity's share of energy use to 35pc by 2035. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: In mid-November 2026, after its ninth consecutive cut, what was the retail price of petrol in Pakistan per litre?
mcqs.explanation: Petrol was cut by Rs2 to Rs330 per litre, while high-speed diesel stayed at Rs360. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, short-term inflation (SPI) for the week ending Nov 12, 2026 stood at what rate year-on-year?
mcqs.explanation: The weekly SPI rose to 11.21pc year-on-year, driven mainly by perishable food items. (Dawn)
